data.why: GeoDFN generates fracture networks purely from statistical parameters entered or loaded via built-in presets (Brazil Apodi, Single Set, Orthogonal set, Conjugate set) baked into app.py's session state; there is no file upload widget and nothing to copy in.

goals: load the 'Brazil Apodi' outcrop-calibrated preset and generate an ensemble of realizations to see geologically plausible fracture patterns
tune fracture-set parameters (intensity, length/orientation/spacing distributions, buffer zone) and regenerate to see how the pattern and stereonet/rose diagram respond
compare multiple fracture sets (e.g. Orthogonal set, Conjugate set presets) and inspect per-set statistics (count, mean length, mean aperture)
choose an aperture model (constant, sub-linear, Barton-Bandis, Lepillier) and check resulting mean aperture values
increase the number of realizations to assess variability across an equiprobable ensemble and note how many converge vs. hit the placement retry limit
download the generated DFN ensemble (coordinates, apertures, stats, images) as a ZIP for use in a flow/transport simulator

review.summary: The tree follows GeoDFN's stated workflow from presets or outcrop statistics through the stress-shadow buffer and aperture model to an exported ensemble, and its features are well cut and confirmed by an independent replay. However, the fracture maps and rose diagrams never rendered, three cited screens don't show what their nodes claim, and domain sizing and parameter-sensitivity comparison are missing, so it needs those fixes before filing.
